description: Any eligible US stock. Second-order effects: events traced to a company the news never names.

positions.thesis: FDA classed Vertex's reply to a late-cycle information request as a major amendment, so the povetacicept IgAN PDUFA moves from 11-30 to no later than 2-28-2027. VRTX fell about 7% (roughly $10B) for a drug JPM puts at $3.4B peak sales with 95% PoA. The core CF franchise is untouched, no safety or efficacy issue was cited, and Vera already has an approved rival, so the first-mover loss is not new. Citi (PT 585) and JPM (PT 570) reiterated. Expect a partial retrace of the overshoot.

sources.answer:
PAGE DATE: Nov 25, 2026

**Why the PDUFA date was extended:** The page says the extension was not a clear-cut "major amendment" from Vertex's side. The FDA issued a late-cycle information request, and Vertex responded promptly. Regulators then classified that response as a major amendment, which is what triggered the delay. The FDA said it needs more time to evaluate the newly submitted data. The article adds that standard PDUFA extensions are usually used when supplemental material could resolve open questions and still allow approval in the current cycle.

**New date:** The Biologics License

causal_chain.step: FDA sent a late-cycle information request; Vertex's response was classed a major amendment, so the povetacicept PDUFA moved from 11-30 to no later than 2-28-2027. No safety or efficacy issue was cited.

The market cut about $10B from VRTX, while JPM values the asset at $3.4B peak sales with 95% PoA and Vera's competing drug has been approved since 7-7-26. Vera's gain is small next to Vertex's loss, so the move is not a competitor transfer. The sell-off looks larger than the delay justifies.

trades.thesis: TJX beat and raised on 11-18 (comps +4% vs plan 2-3%, FY comp now 4%, Marmaxx improved) and Target posted +5.6% comps on +5% traffic. US control retail sales came in at +0.6% vs 0.4%. Ross reports Q3 on 11-19 after the close with 8 straight EPS beats and comps of +7% and +10% in the last two quarters. It fell 4 days into the print and has lagged TJX's rebound. The edge is Ross's own print, since the sympathy gap is already in the fill price.

causal_chain.step: TJX Q3 FY27 (11-18 BMO): comps +4% vs 2-3% plan and 3.8% consensus, FY comp raised to 4%, Marmaxx improved. Target comps +5.6% on +5.0% traffic. Both show strong off-price and value traffic in the Aug-Oct quarter.

Ross competes for the same shopper as Marmaxx, and its quarter ended around Oct 31. Core retail sales beat (+0.6% vs 0.4%), so the same demand should show in Ross's Q3 comps. Ross has beaten EPS 8 of 8 quarters, with consensus EPS about $1.85 on $6.2B revenue.

ROST reports 11-19 after the close, and the reaction lands in my 3-day horizon. Weakest link: TJX's Marmaxx comp was only +2%, so strength may not transfer to Ross. The sympathy gap at today's open is already in my fill price.

trades.thesis: Magnite's blowout Q3 (CTV +39%, political ad spend, raised guide) lifted MGNI 21%, but SSP peer PubMatic only rose 2.6% ahead of its own Q3 print on 11-09 after close. Read-through from strong CTV/political demand suggests upside risk to PubMatic's guide; small size because earnings are binary and PUBM's mix differs.

trades.thesis: Intel guided PC market to decline into 2H27 (Client Computing missed by ~$0.7B); Corsair (PC components/peripherals) reports Q3 on Nov 5 and sector sympathy (HPQ -10% premarket) has not hit CRSR yet, which closed flat/up. Expect cautious guide or sympathy selling into earnings. Weakest link: DRAM-kit price inflation may lift Corsair revenue and offset PC unit weakness.

PAGE DATE: 29/10/2026 (published 9:02 PM; the article's metadata lists the same date, 2026-10-29)

Per the page, Intel said it expects the PC market to decline into the second half of 2027. The page calls this significant for Client Computing, Intel's largest division, which sells processors for personal computers.

On causes, the page gives none. It does not explain why the PC market is expected to shrink.

On client segment weakness, the page reports that Client Computing revenue was about $8.1 billion in Q3, against expectations of roughly $8.8 billion, so it missed estimates. It also says

sessions.feedback: economic_calendar actuals still lag the actual release time, so I used web_search for them. The digest's pre-market mover table is dominated by thin prints; a liquidity filter, for example at least 5% of average daily volume, would make it far more useful. A tool that lists index-deletion candidates, or a pre-market read-across screen for peers of a fresh mover, would help this weird-links style. Some law-firm pages fail in read_page (kelleydrye) while others (hklaw, casrai) work. It would help to know ahead of time which ones fail.

1) economic_calendar did not populate actuals at 13:33 UTC even though the 08:30 ET releases (PCE, GDP) were already out. Its time column is labelled New York but looks like UTC. I had to find the PCE numbers through a web_search snippet. A refresh, or a correct timezone label, would help.
2) get_quotes pre-market data lags about 15 minutes, so at 13:33 UTC the quote predates the 13:30 UTC PCE release. A 'data as of' warning near scheduled releases would help me avoid trading around binary events.
3) read_page fails on many news domains (invezz, kfgo, foxbusiness). That is acceptable because search snippets carry the numbers, but a list of domains known to work would save calls.
4) The 'no ticker in digest headlines' rule combined with pre-open fills means that by the time I see a story, the first-order and sympathy moves are already in the pre-market price. That makes my second-order approach hard to execute on same-day news; the dated-catalyst route (events after the next open) is the only one with an edge.

No blocking issues. Two small requests. (1) Pre-market prices for scan/get_quotes come with a lag, and the open auction price is unknown, so for names that gap on overnight news (SPY -1.5% since the close) I am sizing off stale numbers. (2) An earnings calendar for the coming week, with BMO/AMC and consensus, would save several web searches. The scan 'earnings' field only covers the last two sessions and the next five, and sometimes shows 'time not given'. Also, scan labels SHOE's earnings as 'none' although it reported this morning, so that field misses same-day reports for some tickers.

The research budget ran out before I could write my notes file, so tomorrow's session starts from this summary and the old notes. A small allowance for a notes update after the budget message would help. read_page failed on Yahoo Finance article URLs again. ETFs such as SPY and QQQ don't appear to be tradable, so I can't express a clean market-beta view. A tool that returned a live intraday market snapshot would help on volatile gap days.

Nothing blocked me this session. Two small things: read_page on prnewswire returned only navigation and no release body, so I had to rely on web_search snippets from the code tool. It would also help to know whether a stop that gaps through at the open fills at the open price or at the stop price. That decides whether closing manually into a gap beats letting the stop work.

Nothing blocked me, but two things would help.
1. The digest and news feed lag same-morning earnings. WSM, BABA and WMT prints were only in the news feed or web search, and I had to use web_search to find the WSM numbers. An earnings-results feed with EPS/revenue vs consensus and guidance for companies that reported pre-market would save calls.
2. scan shows pre-market only as a percent and a share count. An indication of whether the pre-market print is from IEX only or all venues would help me judge thin prints.

No blocking problems this session. Two things would have saved time. First, an earnings-consensus field (EPS and revenue expectations, and the typical post-earnings move) in scan, because I had to run web searches for it. Second, a sympathy-gap estimate: pre-market prints under 1,000 shares are too thin to judge the fill price for a read-through trade, and orders fill at the open, so I can't tell how much of the move I'll pay for. web_search is only reachable from inside code_execution and returns a JSON string, which costs extra calls. read_page on Benzinga still fails.

Digest 'biggest pre-market movers' ranks thin prints (100-600 shares) by sd, so most of the list is noise (e.g., KNX -8.5% on 396 shares). Filtering on minimum shares or a percent-of-average-day threshold would save budget. A tool returning the biggest losers and gainers of the previous session (not only gainers) would help find overreactions. A 'peers with earnings dates in the next 5 days' lookup by industry would suit the lagging-peer strategy.

Benzinga pages usually fail in read_page, though the digest links mostly point to Benzinga. Pre-market lists mix thin prints with real moves (e.g. NX -19% in the news roundup versus 0.0% in scan). Some prices look like spin-off artifacts (CTVA 9.43, -90% from 52-week high); a flag for corporate actions would help.

read_page fails on many major sites (CNBC, NBC, gurufocus), which makes the two-source requirement hard. The sandbox does not keep Python state between code_execution cells, so imports have to be repeated in every cell. A pre-market quote that shows volume (e.g. 828 shares) makes thin-volume REIT quotes misleading; a flag for low-volume pre-market prints would help.

The digest has no sector or industry-level sympathy view and the scan's industry labels are coarse (e.g. UBER/LYFT listed as 'Business Services'). Web search returns stale results for some queries. Earnings-call transcripts or a news-by-ticker endpoint would help.

summary:
Session 2026-11-27.

Session 2026-11-27 (Black Friday half-day). Opened one trade: VRTX long 5% (stop -6%, target +7%, 10-day horizon, p=0.55). Equity about $100.5k, otherwise cash.

Tape: SPY pre-market +1.7% and QQQ +2.3%. 11-25 was a V-reversal: NDX fell 4.7% at the open, touched a bear market, and closed -0.65% with AI names closing near their highs. Today's driver is Beijing's national-team pledge (China CSI Semi +17.6%, a record), the SK Hynix buyback doubling and falling yields. I did not chase AI names at the gap-up open: the 11-23 relief rally faded, and tax-loss pressure on the -70% names runs to mid-Dec.

Resolved: the Section 301 text came out on 11-25. It covers 14 economies (Mexico and Norway deferred) with rates of 15-35% that mostly equal prior deals. Sec 232 goods including semis are exempt. Comments are due 1-5-27 and hearings start 1-25, with no effective date. The market shrugged (apparel up 3 days, TXN and ADI rebounded), so there is no near-term trade.

Examined and rejected:
- Altria/Imperial Brands (UK deadline Dec 24; MO -2%, BTI -1.6%; IMBBY ineligible).
- Brazil ADRs (Trabuco finance-minister catch-up already priced).
- Refiners (cracks collapsed, no catalyst).
- Houthi/Hormuz oil.
- DE peers (CNH, AGCO moved 11-25).
- DELL/HPE (+4% pre-market, chase).
- AI-credit and private-credit names (all bouncing, no dislocation).
- Neocloud shorts (squeeze day).

Next session (Mon 11-30):
- Check whether VRTX held its fill (about 523) and what rotation does to defensives.
- OPEC+ meets Sunday.
- Check whether the Friday gap-up held. If AI names close in the upper half on a second day, consider DELL/HPE longs.
- Dec 1: MRVL, NTAP, OKTA earnings; Huang House testimony.
- Dec 2: AEO, FIVE, M.
- Dec 3: Huang Senate testimony, S, PVH.
- Dec 4: jobs report.
- Dec 9: FOMC.
- Dec 11: NDX announcement. Plan to short announced deletions on Dec 14, after checking the rules.
- G20 Miami Dec 14-15 (Vietnam apparel short if no deal).
- Notes updated (general plus VRTX).
notes:
NOTES (updated 2026-11-27)
- Tooling: web_search only works via code_execution and returns a JSON STRING (json.loads it; IMPORT json IN EVERY CELL; results are dicts with title/url/content/page_age). Benzinga/nikkei/bbntimes/substack(sometimes OK: redeyereturns, cnttrading worked 11-27)/marketscreener/invezz/kfgo/foxbusiness/kelleydrye read_page often FAIL; hklaw.com, casrai, investing.com, longbridge, factrail, yahoo, 247wallst, baystreet, tradingview read OK. web_search snippets often carry the numbers. get_quotes/get_history/search_symbols/scan/news work directly. scan's pre-market % on <1,000 shares is noise. economic_calendar 'actual' did NOT refresh at 13:33 UTC: use web_search. Digest 'top pre-market movers' are often thin prints. Code rejects trades whose names appear in digest HEADLINES. news() on tickers gives press-release numbers at ~12:30 UTC. scan 'gap %' vs 'close in range' shows intraday reversals (11-25: gap -5 to -9% on AI names, close in range 0.9+).
- Macro regime (Nov 2026): 10y ~4.85% (fell 30bp in 8 sessions, bull flattener), Fed funds 3.75-4.00, Dec 9 hike ~priced (Waller floated 50bp), Jan hike maybe. Oct PCE core 3.3% y/y, Q3 GDP 4.3%. Iran war since Feb; oil: Brent ~96.5 (up from 90) after Houthi hits on Ras Tanura/Jazan refineries 11-25/26 and two tankers mined in Hormuz 11-26; OPEC+ meets Sun 11-29. Refiner cracks collapsed from record 3-2-1 $81.9 (9-25) to ~$34; VLO/MPC/PSX/DK 8-day losing streaks, -30% from highs (no trade).
- AI bust: NDX -20 to -23% from Oct high, 11-25 NDX fell 4.7% in first 15 min (touched bear market) then closed -0.65% (options/dealer hedging, CTA/short-covering, 'leverage not news'). Chips lagged: NVDA -3.9% (S&P put AA on CreditWatch neg), MU low -13% closed -4.5%, ORCL 52w low (CDS 360bp). 11-27 pre-market: SPY +1.7%, QQQ +2.3%, NVDA +2.6%, MU +5.9%, SNDK +10%, CRWV +5%, NBIS +7%; DRIVER: Beijing State Council 'national team' pledge made China CSI Semiconductor index +17.6% (record), STAR50 +15% on 11-27 Asia hours, SK Hynix doubled daily buyback (700k sh), Deutsche: 'tech selloff stabilised'. Systematic funds will not add until 2% daily moves stop being normal. November on track to be worst since 2008. NOT chased at the 11-27 open (pre-open gap = fill price; 11-23 relief rally opened at high and faded two days). Tax-loss selling pressure on -70% AI names likely through mid-Dec.
- SECTION 301 (resolved 11-25): USTR proposed 'structural excess capacity' tariffs on 14 economies (Mexico and Norway deferred): EU/Japan/Korea/Taiwan/Switzerland up to 15%, SG up to 20% (10% with pact), IN 25% (17%), VN 35% (20% with pact), ASEAN others 18%, China up to 20% on top of old 301. Goods under Sec 232 (steel, aluminum, copper, autos, semis, pharma) EXEMPT. Replaces the July 2026 forced-labor 301 (10-12.5%). Comments due Jan 5 2027, hearings Jan 25, no effective date; G20 Miami Dec 14-15 may bring deals. Market shrugged: apparel/footwear (VFC, COLM, CROX, NKE, LULU) up 3 days in a row; TXN +4.5%, ADI +6.4% rebounded. Not a near-term trade; possible VN-exposed apparel short only if G20 deals fail (not before Dec 15).
- DELL/HPE: Dell beat/raise 11-24 (EPS 9.45, FY27 29.68, $25B buyback) still sold; both +3.5-4% pre-market 11-27 (DELL ~309, HPE ~42). HPQ +11.5% on 11-25 FY27 guide; CDW +6.6%. No position.
- Peer lags already priced: DE +4.4% (11-25 BMO, trough call) with CNH +8%, AGCO +4%, ALG +3.5% same day; TITN reported 11-24.
- ALTRIA/IMPERIAL (11-26): MO confirmed considering all-cash bid for Imperial Brands (mkt cap ~GBP26.8B, shares +14-17%) and talks with a third party (JT reported) to take part of the assets (likely US assets for FTC). UK put-up-or-shut-up deadline Dec 24. MO -2.3% pre-market (leverage), BTI -1.6%, PM -0.7%. IMBBY not eligible. No trade (50/50 either way for acquirer).
- ROTATION: 11-24 health care/staples led; 11-27 pre-market XLV +0.07% and XLP -0.16% vs SPY +1.7% (defensives lag in risk-on).
- ANT: IPO 83, 11-25 low ~74, closed 82.79, pre-market +4%. NDX fast-entry: announcement after close Dec 11, entry Dec 21 (funds buy at close Dec 18). NDX reconstitution Dec 11: PLAN = on the Dec 14 session consider shorting announced NDX deletions (small/mid caps like LULU, CDW-type names that fell below rank ~125) into the Dec 18 index-fund sale; check rules first.
- Other dated: NTAP, MRVL, OKTA 12-01 AMC; Huang House testimony 12-01, Senate 12-03; AEO, FIVE, M 12-02; PVH, S 12-03; jobs 12-04; FOMC 12-09; NDX 12-11; G20 Miami 12-14/15; NKE ~12-18; MU mid-Dec.
- VRTX (new 11-27): FDA late-cycle information request -> response classed 'major amendment' -> povetacicept IgAN PDUFA moved from 11-30 to <=2-28-2027. VRTX -7.2% (about $10B erased; JPM peak sales $3.4B at 95% PoA, PT 570; Citi PT 585). VERA +16% (already approved 7-7-26, Trutakna). Long 5% as overreaction fade.
- Trades so far: PUBM (11-06 long 4%, closed 11-13 +12.5%). ROST (11-18 long 4% at 226.23, closed 11-20 ~-8%). VRTX long opened 11-27. No-trade sessions: 10-29, 11-04, 11-16, 11-17, 11-19, 11-20, 11-23, 11-24, 11-25.
- LESSONS:
 1) Peer-earnings-lag longs: PUBM worked (dated catalyst, peer lagged), ROST failed (11-18 buy -> 11-20 print). Retail print reactions follow the NEXT-quarter guide, not the FY raise.
 2) By the pre-open session, first-order and obvious second-order moves are priced (GDS -14.7% a day before I looked; cyber peers +4-6% on PANW; DE peers 11-25; TXN -11% on Section 301 then +4.5% when the real text came). The sympathy gap is in the fill price. Real edge needs dated catalysts AHEAD of the next session.
 3) Regulatory proposals (CRUSH) and big-cap drops can stay down for months: need a catalyst, not just a drop (UNH).
 4) In capitulation tapes pre-open 'bounce' longs are coin flips; wait for stabilisation. 11-25 supplied the first V-reversal; 11-27 gap-up is a chase.
 5) Binary info arriving before my next open (PCE 11-25, DELL AMC 11-24): waiting a day is cheaper than holding through.
 6) Pre-market prints can understate continuation on gap-down days (HPE -12% pre, -16.3% close) AND understate reversals (11-25 AI names gapped -5 to -9%, closed near highs). Pre-market is not the day's extreme in either direction.
 7) Headline policy shocks (Section 301 leak) priced harder than the actual text; read the text, it is often milder (semis exempt under 232, rates equal prior deals). Leak-day sell-offs in the named 'victims' were then reversed.
- Open ideas: NDX deletion shorts Dec 14; HPE/DELL long on a confirmed stabilised tape (8x EPS, buybacks); neocloud shorts only after squeeze to CRWV 55+/NBIS 110; ANT around Dec 11-18; tower churn; JBS/China beef; MA-exposed clinic landlords; NKE into Dec 18; DG print early Dec; biotech M&A read-across after Sanofi/Insmed; Vietnam-apparel short after G20 if deals fail; MO if firm Imperial bid leverages balance sheet.

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is weird, second-order research.

Everyone else reads the headline and trades the company in it. You trade the company the headline
does not mention. Start from events in the news and follow the consequences outward: suppliers,
customers, competitors, substitutes, regions, commodities, logistics, weather, regulation, the
odd dependency nobody has priced. A storm hits the region that grows potatoes for a fast-food chain;
which other chain gains, which frozen-food maker loses, which railroad hauls the replacement crop?

- Every new position, long or short, needs a causal chain of at least two steps from the event to
  the company you trade, each step with a source where possible. Code rejects a trade whose ticker
  or company name appears in today's digest headlines, so the link has to be one you found. The
  losers at the end of a chain are as fair game as the winners: short them.
- Borderline delusional is the brief, but the chain still has to be real: each step should be
  something you could defend with evidence. Write down the step most likely to be wrong.
- Spreading across several smaller bets suits this style better than one big one. Small companies
  cost more to trade, so make the expected move worth it.
- Use search_symbols to find the companies at the end of a chain. Read their exposure, do not assume it.
